title: Investigating Oxidation Mechanisms of Polycrystalline Co/Ni-Base Superalloys using Correlative 4D-STEM and APT
content: Ni-base superalloys are selected when high temperature strength, toughness and oxidation resistance are required. The increasing demand for high-performance materials in extreme environments, such as gas turbines, therefore necessitates the development of advanced superalloys with superior oxidation resistance. The present work focuses on a new generation of polycrystalline Co/Ni-base superalloys, designed for improved thermal stability and oxidation resistance compared to conventional Ni-base alloys. Correlative 4D-Scanning Transmission Electron Microscopy (4D-STEM), electron spectroscopy, and atom probe tomography (APT) were used to link the local structural and chemical variations within the complex interfaces of these oxidized alloys [1,2]. Electron energy loss spectroscopy (EELS) combined with 4D-STEM can be used to differentiate between unique oxide structures such as the Ti oxides such as rutile and anatase. Thus, using advanced correlative microscopy, we could probe the relationship between oxidation behavior and structural evolution by examining specific oxidation states and oxide layer formation under high-temperature stress.
